To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) DXA at the femoral is the most extensively validated and the most widely used technique for assessing osteoporosis; 2) the NHANES reference range should be used to define osteopenia, low bone mass and osteoporosis; and 3) the same cut-off for femoral BMD should be used to diagnose osteoporosis in both women and men.

the World Health Organization (WHO) diagnostic criteria for osteopenia and osteoporosis are based on bone mineral measurements at the femoral-neck made with dual-energy Xray absorptiometry and the reference range is the average BMD in women aged 30 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement and management of osteoporosis and the associated fracture risk.
the development of an algorithm for the diagnosis of primary hyperparathyroidism in postmenopausal women.
the development of a reference standard for the diagnosis of low bone mass and osteoporosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DXA measurement of BMD at the femoral-neck is the reference standard for the assessment of osteoporosis and should be the first-line investigation in all clinical settings.
the diagnosis of osteoperosis in both men and women is based on the measurement of BMD at the femoral shaft by DXA.
osteoporosis should be defined as a systemic skeletal disease characterized by compromised bone strength, with a consequent increase in bone fragility and risk of fracture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have a reference standard for osteoporosis that is based on a well-established technology.
the WHO definition of osteoporosis is based on BMD measurements made at the femur neck with dual-energy x-ray absorptiometric technology.
the reference standard for osteoporosis should be based on the measurement of BMD at the femoral with DXA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need a common standard for the definition of osteoporosis and the diagnosis of osteopenia.

the use of DXA as the reference standard for describing bone density and osteoporosis will facilitate the comparison of the diagnostic performance of different techniques and will provide an evidence base for the adoption of the most appropriate technique for the assessment of bone health in clinical practice.
the femoral neck is a good reference site for defining osteoporosis.
